children.text: oṃ haṭhayogagorakṣaśatakaprārambhaḥ
children.translated_text: Om. The beginning of the hundred verses of <s>Gorakṣa</s> on <s>haṭhayoga</s>.

children.text: śrīguruṃ paramānandaṃ vande svānandavigraham
children.translated_text: I bow to the glorious guru, supreme bliss, whose form is his own bliss,

children.text: yasya sāṃnidhyamātreṇa cidānandāyate tanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: by whose mere presence the body becomes consciousness and bliss.

children.text: antarniścalitātmadīpakalikāsvādhārabandhādibhiḥ yo yogī yugakalpakālakalanāt tvaṃ jajegīyate
children.translated_text: I constantly worship that glorious <s>Mīnanātha</s>, by whose inner steadying of the flame of the self through the root lock and other practices, and by whom the yogin is praised as victorious over the reckoning of ages and cosmic time,

children.text: jñānāmodamahodadhiḥ samabhavad yatrādināthaḥ svayaṃ vyaktāvyaktaguṇādhikaṃ tam aniśaṃ śrīmīnanāthaṃ bhaje ||
children.translated_text: where <s>Ādinātha</s> himself became a great ocean fragrant with knowledge, beyond manifest and unmanifest qualities.

children.text: namaskṛtya guruṃ bhaktyā gorakṣo jñānam uttamam
children.translated_text: Having bowed with devotion to the guru, <s>Gorakṣa</s> speaks the highest knowledge,

children.text: abhīṣṭaṃ yogināṃ brūte paramānandakārakam ||
children.translated_text: desired by yogins and productive of supreme bliss.

children.text: gorakṣaḥ śatakaṃ vakti yogināṃ hitakāmyayā
children.translated_text: <s>Gorakṣa</s> teaches a hundred verses out of desire for the welfare of yogins;

children.text: dhruvaṃ yasyāvabodhena jāyate paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: by understanding them, the supreme state is surely attained.

children.text: etad vimuktisopānam etat kālasya vañcanam
children.translated_text: This is the stairway to liberation; this is the cheating of Time:

children.text: yad vyāvṛttaṃ mano mohād āsaktaṃ paramātmani ||
children.translated_text: the mind, turned away from delusion, is fixed upon the supreme self.

children.text: dvijasevitaśākhasya śrutikalpataroḥ phalam
children.translated_text: The good person cultivates yoga, the fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree of revelation, whose branches are served by twice-born men,

children.text: śamanaṃ bhavatāpasya yogaṃ bhajati sajjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the pacification of the burning pain of worldly existence.

children.text: āsanaṃ prāṇasaṃyāmaḥ pratyāhāro 'tha dhāraṇā
children.translated_text: Posture, restraint of the breath, withdrawal, then concentration,

children.text: dhyānaṃ samādhir etāni yogāṅgāni bhavanti ṣaṭ ||
children.translated_text: meditation, and samādhi: these are the six limbs of yoga.

children.text: āsanāni tu tāvanti yāvatyo jīvajātayaḥ
children.translated_text: There are as many postures as there are kinds of living beings;

children.text: eteṣām akhilān bhedān vijānāti maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maheśvara</s> knows all their distinctions.

children.text: caturāśītilakṣāṇāṃ ekam ekam udāhṛtam
children.translated_text: Of the eighty-four hundred-thousands, one of each has been taught;

children.text: tataḥ śivena pīṭhānāṃ ṣoḍaśānāṃ śataṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Śiva</s> made sixteen hundred seats.

children.text: āsanebhyaḥ samastebhyo dvayam eva viśiṣyate
children.translated_text: Among all the postures, just two are distinguished:

children.text: ekaṃ siddhāsanaṃ proktaṃ dvitīyaṃ kamalāsanam ||
children.translated_text: one is called <s>siddhāsana</s>, and the second is the lotus posture.

children.text: yonisthānakam aṅghrimūlaghaṭitaṃ kṛtvā dṛḍhaṃ vinyasen meḍhre pādam athaikam eva niyataṃ kṛtvā samaṃ vigraham
children.translated_text: Placing the heel firmly at the place of the yoni, one should set one foot steadily at the penis and make the body even.

children.text: sthāṇuḥ saṃyamitendriyo 'caladṛśā paśyan bhruvor antaram etan mokṣakavāṭabhedajanakaṃ siddhāsanaṃ procyate ||
children.translated_text: Like a post, with the senses restrained, gazing motionlessly between the eyebrows: this is called <s>siddhāsana</s>, which brings about the breaking open of the door of liberation.

children.text: vāmorūpari dakṣiṇaṃ hi caraṇaṃ saṃsthāpya vāmaṃ tathā dakṣorūpari paścimena vidhinā dhṛtvā karābhyāṃ dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Having placed the right foot on the left thigh, and likewise the left on the right thigh, holding them firmly with both hands in the reverse manner,

children.text: aṅguṣṭhau hṛdaye nidhāya cibukaṃ nāsāgram ālokayed etad vyādhivikārahāri yamināṃ padmāsanaṃ procyate ||
children.translated_text: placing the thumbs at the heart, setting the chin down, one should look at the tip of the nose. This is called <s>padmāsana</s> for disciplined practitioners, removing disease and disorder.

children.text: ṣaṭcakraṃ ṣoḍaśādhāraṃ trilakṣaṃ vyomapañcakam
children.translated_text: The six cakras, the sixteen supports, the three goals, and the five spaces:

children.text: svadehe ye na jānanti kathaṃ sidhyanti yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how can yogins who do not know these in their own body attain success?

children.text: ekastambhaṃ navadvāraṃ gṛhaṃ pañcādhidaivatam
children.translated_text: The body is a house with one pillar, nine doors, and five presiding deities;

children.text: svadehaṃ ye na jānanti kathaṃ sidhyanti yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how can yogins who do not know their own body attain success?

children.text: caturdalaṃ syād ādhāraḥ svādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca ṣaḍdalam
children.translated_text: The support has four petals, and <s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s> has six petals;

children.text: nābhau daśadalaṃ padmaṃ sūryasaṃkhyadalaṃ hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: at the navel is a ten-petaled lotus, and at the heart one with as many petals as the number of the suns, that is twelve.

children.text: kaṇṭhe syāt ṣoḍaśadalaṃ bhrūmadhye dvidalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: At the throat there is one with sixteen petals, and between the eyebrows one with two petals;

children.text: sahasradalam ākhyātaṃ brahmarandhre mahāpathe ||
children.translated_text: the thousand-petaled lotus is said to be at the <s>brahmarandhra</s>, on the great path.

children.text: ādhāraḥ prathamaṃ cakraṃ svādhiṣṭhānaṃ dvitīyakam
children.translated_text: The first cakra is the support; <s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s> is the second.

children.text: yonisthānaṃ dvayor madhye kāmarūpaṃ nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: Between the two, at the place of the yoni, is said to be <s>Kāmarūpa</s>.

children.text: ādhārākhyaṃ gudasthānaṃ paṅkajaṃ ca caturdalam
children.translated_text: The place of the anus, called the support, is a four-petaled lotus;

children.text: tanmadhye procyate yoniḥ kāmākṣā siddhavanditā ||
children.translated_text: in its middle is taught the yoni, <s>Kāmākṣā</s>, worshiped by siddhas.

children.text: yonimadhye mahāliṅgaṃ paścimābhimukhaṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: In the middle of the yoni stands the great liṅga, facing west;

children.text: mastake maṇivad bimbaṃ yo jānāti sa yogavit ||
children.translated_text: one who knows the jewel-like orb at its head is a knower of yoga.

children.text: taptacāmīkarābhāsaṃ taḍillekheva visphurat
children.translated_text: Shining like heated gold, flashing like a streak of lightning,

children.text: trikoṇaṃ tatpuraṃ vahner adho meḍhrāt pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: that triangular city of fire is established below the penis.

children.text: yat samādhau paraṃ jyotir anantaṃ viśvatomukham
children.translated_text: When, in samādhi, that supreme light, endless and facing in every direction,

children.text: tasmin dṛṣṭe mahāyoge yātāyātaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: is seen in great yoga, there is no coming and going.

children.text: svaśabdena bhavet prāṇaḥ svādhiṣṭhānaṃ tadāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: By the word sva is meant prāṇa; its seat is <s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s>.

children.text: svādhiṣṭhānāt padād asmān meḍhram evābhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: From this word <s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s>, the penis itself is designated.

children.text: tantunā maṇivat proto yatra kandaḥ suṣumṇayā
children.translated_text: Where the bulb is strung on the <s>suṣumṇā</s> like a jewel on a thread,

children.text: tannābhimaṇḍalaṃ cakraṃ procyate maṇipūrakam ||
children.translated_text: that cakra in the region of the navel is called <s>maṇipūraka</s>.

children.text: dvādaśāre mahācakre puṇyapāpavivarjite
children.translated_text: In the great twelve-spoked wheel, beyond merit and demerit,

children.text: tāvaj jīvo bhramaty eva yāvat tattvaṃ na vindati ||
children.translated_text: the individual soul keeps wandering only so long as it does not find reality.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ meḍhrād adho nābheḥ kandayoniḥ khagāṇḍavat
children.translated_text: Above the penis and below the navel is the bulb-yoni, like a bird’s egg;

children.text: tatra nāḍyaḥ samutpannāḥ sahasrāṇāṃ dvisaptatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: there the nāḍīs arise, seventy-two thousand in number.

children.text: teṣu nāḍisahasreṣu dvisaptatir udāhṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Among those thousands of nāḍīs, seventy-two are taught;

children.text: pradhānaṃ prāṇavāhinyo bhūyas tatra daśa smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as principal carriers of prāṇa, ten among them are especially remembered.

children.text: iḍā ca piṅgalā caiva suṣumṇā ca tṛtīyakā
children.translated_text: <s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, and <s>Suṣumṇā</s> as the third,

children.text: gāndhārī hastijihvā ca pūṣā caiva yaśasvinī ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Hastijihvā</s>, <s>Pūṣā</s>, and also <s>Yaśasvinī</s>;

children.text: alambuṣā kuhūś caiva śaṅkhinī daśamī smṛtā
children.translated_text: <s>Alambuṣā</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>, and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> is remembered as the tenth.

children.text: etan nāḍimayaṃ cakraṃ jñātavyaṃ yogibhiḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: This cakra made of nāḍīs should always be known by yogins.

children.text: iḍā vāme sthitā bhāge piṅgalā dakṣiṇe tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Iḍā</s> is situated on the left side, and <s>Piṅgalā</s> on the right;

children.text: suṣumṇā madhyadeśe tu gāndhārī vāmacakṣuṣi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Suṣumṇā</s> is in the middle region, and <s>Gāndhārī</s> in the left eye.

children.text: dakṣiṇe hastijihvā ca pūṣā karṇe ca dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: <s>Hastijihvā</s> is in the right eye, and <s>Pūṣā</s> in the right ear;

children.text: yaśasvinī vāmakarṇe cāsane vāpy alambuṣā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yaśasvinī</s> is in the left ear, and <s>Alambuṣā</s> is at the seat.

children.text: kuhūś ca liṅgadeśe tu mūlasthāne ca śaṅkhinī
children.translated_text: <s>Kuhū</s> is in the region of the liṅga, and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> at the root-place.

children.text: evaṃ dvāram upāśritya tiṣṭhanti daśanāḍikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the ten nāḍīs stand, taking support in the doors.

children.text: iḍāpiṅgalāsuṣumṇā ca tisro nāḍya udāhṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, and <s>Suṣumṇā</s> are declared to be the three nāḍīs

children.text: satataṃ prāṇavāhinyaḥ somasūryāgnidevatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: that constantly carry prāṇa and have the moon, sun, and fire as their deities.

children.text: prāṇo 'pānaḥ samānaś codāno vyānau ca vāyavaḥ
children.translated_text: The vital winds are prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna,

children.text: nāgaḥ kūrmo 'tha kṛkaro devadatto dhanaṃjayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, <s>Kṛkara</s>, <s>Devadatta</s>, and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.

children.text: hṛdi prāṇo vasen nityam apāno gudamaṇḍale
children.translated_text: Prāṇa always resides in the heart, and apāna in the region of the anus;

children.text: samāno nābhideśe syād udānaḥ kaṇṭhamadhyagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: samāna is in the region of the navel, and udāna is located in the middle of the throat.

children.text: udgāre nāgākhyātaḥ kūrma unmīlane smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: In belching it is called <s>Nāga</s>; in opening the eyes <s>Kūrma</s> is remembered.

children.text: kṛkaraḥ kṣutakṛj jñeyo devadatto vijṛmbhaṇe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛkara</s> should be known as causing hunger, and <s>Devadatta</s> in yawning.

children.text: na jahāti mṛtaṃ cāpi sarvavyāpi dhanaṃjayaḥ
children.translated_text: And the all-pervading <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> does not leave even a dead body.

children.text: ete sarvāsu nāḍīṣu bhramante jīvarūpiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These, in the form of the living being, wander in all the nāḍīs (channels).

children.text: ākṣipto bhujadaṇḍena yathoccalati kandukaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as a ball, struck by the arm as by a rod, springs upward,

children.text: prāṇāpānasamākṣiptas tathā jīvo na tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: so the living being, driven by <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, does not remain still.

children.text: prāṇāpānavaśo jīvo hy adhaś cordhvaṃ ca dhāvati
children.translated_text: The living being, under the control of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, runs downward and upward,

children.text: vāmadakṣiṇamārgeṇa cañcalatvān na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: and because of its restlessness along the left and right paths, it is not seen.

children.text: rajjubaddho yathā śyeno gato 'py ākṛṣyate
children.translated_text: Just as a falcon tied with a cord, even when it has gone, is drawn back,

children.text: guṇabaddhas tathā jīvaḥ prāṇāpānena kṛṣyate ||
children.translated_text: so the living being, bound by the guṇas, is pulled by <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>.

children.text: apānaḥ karṣati prāṇaṃ prāṇo 'pānaṃ ca karṣati
children.translated_text: <s>Apāna</s> draws <s>prāṇa</s>, and <s>prāṇa</s> draws <s>apāna</s>.

children.text: ūrdhvādhaḥ saṃsthitāv etau saṃyojayati yogavit ||
children.translated_text: These two, situated above and below, the knower of yoga joins together.

children.text: hakāreṇa bahir yāti sakāreṇa viśet punaḥ
children.translated_text: With the syllable ha it goes out; with the syllable sa it enters again.

children.text: haṃsa haṃsety amuṃ mantraṃ jīvo japati sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: The living being always recites this mantra, 'haṃsa, haṃsa.'

children.text: ṣaṭśatāni tv ahorātre sahasrāṇy ekaviṃśatiḥ
children.translated_text: Six hundred by day and night, and twenty-one thousand more,

children.text: etat saṃkhyānvitaṃ mantraṃ jīvo japati sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: with this number the living being always recites the mantra.

children.text: ajapā nāma gāyatrī yogināṃ mokṣadāyinī
children.translated_text: This <s>ajapā</s> (unrecited) <s>Gāyatrī</s> gives liberation to yogins.

children.text: asyāḥ saṃkalpamātreṇa sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: By the mere intention toward it, one is freed from all sins.

children.text: anayā sadṛśī vidyā anayā sadṛśo japaḥ
children.translated_text: There has been no knowledge equal to this, no recitation equal to this,

children.text: anayā sadṛśaṃ jñānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: no wisdom equal to this, nor will there be in the future.

children.text: kuṇḍalinyāḥ samudbhūtā gāyatrī prāṇadhāriṇī
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s>, arisen from <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, sustains the breaths.

children.text: prāṇavidyā mahāvidyā yas tāṃ vetti sa yogavit ||
children.translated_text: It is the knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s>, the great knowledge; whoever knows it is a knower of yoga.

children.text: kandordhvaṃ kuṇḍalī śaktir aṣṭadhā kuṇḍalākṛti
children.translated_text: Above the kanda is <s>Kuṇḍalī Śakti</s>, coiled in eight coils,

children.text: brahmadvāramukhaṃ nityaṃ mukhenācchādya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: always covering the mouth of the brahma-door with her mouth.

children.text: yena dvāreṇa gantavyaṃ brahmasthānam anāmayam
children.translated_text: The door by which one must go to the stainless place of brahman,

children.text: mukhenācchādya tad dvāraṃ prasuptā parameśvarī ||
children.translated_text: that door the supreme goddess covers with her mouth, asleep.

children.text: prabuddhā vahniyogena manasā mārutāhatā
children.translated_text: Awakened by the yoga of fire and struck by the wind through the mind,

children.text: sūcīvad guṇam ādāya vrajaty ūrdhvaṃ suṣumṇayā ||
children.translated_text: taking up the thread like a needle, she goes upward through <s>suṣumṇā</s>.

children.text: prasphuradbhujagākārā padmatantunibhā śubhā
children.translated_text: She is auspicious, shaped like a flashing serpent, like the fibre of a lotus stalk.

children.text: prabuddhā vahniyogena vratya ūrdhvaṃ suṣumṇayā ||
children.translated_text: Awakened by the yoga of fire, she goes upward through <s>suṣumṇā</s>.

children.text: udghaṭayet kapāṭaṃ tu yathā kuñcikayā haṭhāt
children.translated_text: As one would forcefully open a door-panel with a key,

children.text: kuṇḍalinyā tathā yogī mokṣadvāraṃ prabhedayet ||
children.translated_text: so the yogin should pierce the door of liberation by means of <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā saṃpuṭitau karau dṛḍhataraṃ baddhvā tu padmāsanaṃ gāḍhaṃ vakṣasi saṃnidhāya cibukaṃ dhyātvā ca tat prekṣitam
children.translated_text: Having made the hands into a closed cup, firmly bound the lotus posture, set the chin tightly on the chest, and meditated on that which is to be seen,

children.text: vāraṃ vāram apānam ūrdhvam anilaṃ proccārayet pūritaṃ muñcan prāṇam upaiti bodham atulaṃ śaktiprabodhān naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: again and again he should raise <s>apāna</s> upward and impel the filled wind; releasing <s>prāṇa</s>, a man attains incomparable awakening through the awakening of śakti.

children.text: aṅgānāṃ mardanaṃ kuryāc chramajātena vāriṇā
children.translated_text: He should massage the limbs with the water produced by exertion,

children.text: kaṭvamlalavaṇatyāgī kṣīrabhojanam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: and, abandoning pungent, sour, and salty foods, he should take milk as food.

children.text: brahmacārī mitāhārī tyāgī yogaparāyaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Celibate, moderate in food, renunciant, and devoted to yoga,

children.text: abdād ūrdhvaṃ bhavet siddho nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: after a year he becomes perfected; no deliberation is to be made about this.

children.text: susnigdhaṃ madhurāhāraṃ caturthāṃśavivarjitam
children.translated_text: Food that is very unctuous and sweet, with a fourth part left out,

children.text: bhujyate surasamprītyai mitāhāraḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: is eaten for the pleasure of the gods; that is called <s>mitāhāra</s> (moderate diet).

children.text: kandordhvaṃ kuṇḍalī śaktir aṣṭadhā kuṇḍalākṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Above the kanda is <s>Kuṇḍalī Śakti</s>, coiled in eight coils,

children.text: bandhanāya ca mūḍhānāṃ yogināṃ mokṣadā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: remembered as causing bondage for fools and giving liberation to yogins.

children.text: mahāmudrāṃ namomudrām uḍḍiyānaṃ jalaṃdharam
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāmudrā</s>, <s>namomudrā</s>, <s>uḍḍiyāna</s>, <s>jalaṃdhara</s>,

children.text: mūlabandhaṃ ca yo vetti sa yogī siddhibhājanam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>mūlabandha</s>: whoever knows these is a yogin, a vessel of siddhi.

children.text: śodhanaṃ nāḍijālasya cālanaṃ candrasūryayoḥ
children.translated_text: The purification of the network of nāḍīs, the setting in motion of moon and sun,

children.text: rasānāṃ śoṣaṇaṃ caiva mahāmudrābhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and the drying up of the fluids: this is called <s>mahāmudrā</s>.

children.text: vakṣonyastahanur nipīḍya suciraṃ yoniṃ ca vāmāṅghriṇā hastābhyām avadhāritaṃ prasāritaṃ pādaṃ tathā dakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: With the chin placed on the chest, pressing the yoni for a long time with the left foot, and with the hands holding the right foot stretched out,

children.text: āpūrya śvasanena kukṣiyugalaṃ baddhvā śanai recayed eṣā pātakanāśinī sumahatī mudrā nṝṇāṃ procyate ||
children.translated_text: having filled both sides of the belly with breath and bound it, he should exhale slowly; this is proclaimed the very great, sin-destroying mudrā for human beings.

children.text: candrāṅgena samabhyasya sūryāṅgenābhyaset punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having practiced it with the lunar limb, he should practice again with the solar limb,

children.text: yāvat tulyā bhavet saṃkhyā tato mudrāṃ visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: until the number becomes equal; then he should release the mudrā.

children.text: na hi pathyam apathyaṃ vā rasāḥ sarve 'pi nīrasāḥ
children.translated_text: For him there is neither wholesome nor unwholesome food; all tastes are tasteless.

children.text: api muktaṃ viṣaṃ ghoraṃ pīyūṣam api jīryate ||
children.translated_text: Even a terrible poison, once released, is digested like nectar.

children.text: kṣayakuṣṭhagudāvartagulmājīrṇapurogamāḥ
children.translated_text: Wasting disease, skin disease, gudāvarta, abdominal tumors, indigestion, and the rest:

children.text: tasya doṣāḥ kṣayaṃ yānti mahāmudrāṃ tu yo 'bhyaset ||
children.translated_text: the disorders of one who practices <s>mahāmudrā</s> go to destruction.

children.text: kathiteyaṃ mahāmudrā mahāsiddhikarā nṝṇām
children.translated_text: This <s>mahāmudrā</s> has been taught as producing great siddhi for human beings.

children.text: gopanīyā prayatnena na deyā yasya kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: It is to be carefully kept secret; it is not to be given to just anyone.

children.text: kapālakuhare jihvā praviṣṭā viparītagā
children.translated_text: When the tongue has entered the hollow of the skull, turned backward,

children.text: bhruvor antargatā dṛṣṭir mudrā bhavati khecarī ||
children.translated_text: and the gaze is fixed between the eyebrows, the mudrā is <s>khecarī</s>.

children.text: na rogo maraṇaṃ tandrā na nidrā na kṣudhā tṛṣā
children.translated_text: There is no disease, death, torpor, sleep, hunger, or thirst,

children.text: na ca mūrchā bhavet tasya yo mudrāṃ vetti khecarīm ||
children.translated_text: nor fainting, for the one who knows the <s>khecarī</s> mudrā.

children.text: pīḍyate na sa rogeṇa lipyate na ca karmaṇā
children.translated_text: He is not afflicted by disease, nor is he stained by karma.

children.text: bādhyate na sa kālena yo mudrāṃ vetti khecarīm ||
children.translated_text: He is not oppressed by Time, who knows the <s>khecarī</s> mudrā.

children.text: cittaṃ carati khe yasmāj jihvā carati khe gatā
children.translated_text: Because the mind moves in space and the tongue, gone there, moves in space,

children.text: tenaiṣā khecarī nāma mudrā siddhair nirūpitā ||
children.translated_text: therefore this mudrā is called <s>khecarī</s>, as defined by the siddhas.

children.text: bindumālaṃ śarīraṃ tu śirās tatra pratiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: The body is a mass of bindu, and the channels are established there.

children.text: bhāvayanti śarīraṃ yā āpādatalamastakam ||
children.translated_text: They permeate the body from the soles of the feet to the head.

children.text: khecaryā mudritaṃ yena vivaraṃ lambikordhvataḥ
children.translated_text: For the one by whom the aperture above the uvula is sealed by <s>khecarī</s>,

children.text: na tasya kṣarate binduḥ kāminyāliṅgitasya ca ||
children.translated_text: his bindu does not flow away, even when he is embraced by a passionate woman.

children.text: yāvad binduḥ sthito dehe tāvat kālabhayaṃ kutaḥ
children.translated_text: So long as bindu remains in the body, how can there be fear of Time?

children.text: yāvad baddhā nabhomudrā tāvad bindur na gacchati ||
children.translated_text: So long as the sky-mudrā is bound, so long bindu does not go away.

children.text: calito 'pi yadā binduḥ samprāptaś ca hutāśanam
children.translated_text: Even when the bindu has moved and has reached the fire,

children.text: vrajaty ūrdhvaṃ hṛtaḥ śaktyā niruddho yonimudrayā ||
children.translated_text: carried upward by śakti and restrained by <s>yonimudrā</s>.

children.text: sa punar dvividho binduḥ pāṇḍuro lohitas tathā
children.translated_text: That bindu is again of two kinds: white and red.

children.text: pāṇḍuraṃ śukram ity āhur lohitaṃ tu mahārajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They call the white one semen, but the red one is <s>rajas</s>, O great king.

children.text: sindūradravasaṃkāśaṃ ravisthāne sthitaṃ rajaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>rajas</s>, resembling a stream of vermilion, is situated in the place of the sun;

children.text: śaśisthāne sthito bindus tayor aikyaṃ sudurlabham ||
children.translated_text: the bindu is situated in the place of the moon. The union of the two is very difficult to attain.

children.text: binduḥ śivo rajaḥ śaktir bindum indū rajo raviḥ
children.translated_text: Bindu is <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>rajas</s> is <s>Śakti</s>; bindu is the moon and <s>rajas</s> is the sun.

children.text: ubhayoḥ saṃgamād eva prāpyate paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: Only from the conjunction of the two is the supreme state obtained.

children.text: vāyunā śakticāreṇa preritaṃ tu mahārajaḥ
children.translated_text: And when, by the movement of śakti, it is impelled by the wind, O great king,

children.text: bindunaiti sahaikatvaṃ bhaved divyaṃ vapus tadā ||
children.translated_text: the <s>rajas</s> comes into oneness with bindu; then the body becomes divine.

children.text: śukraṃ candreṇa saṃyuktaṃ rajaḥ sūryeṇa saṃyutam
children.translated_text: Semen is joined with the moon, and <s>rajas</s> is joined with the sun.

children.text: tayoḥ samarasaikatvaṃ yo jānāti sa yogavit ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the single sameness of flavor of the two is a knower of yoga.

children.text: uḍḍīnaṃ kurute yasmād aviśrāntaṃ mahākhagaḥ
children.translated_text: Because the great bird continually makes its flight upward,

children.text: uḍḍīyānaṃ tad eva syāt tava bandho'bhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: that very thing is <s>uḍḍīyāna</s>; your bandha is so called.

children.text: udarāt paścime bhāge hy adho nābher nigadyate
children.translated_text: It is taught as being at the western part of the belly, below the navel.

children.text: uḍḍīyanasya bandho 'yaṃ tatra bandho vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: This is the bandha of <s>uḍḍīyāna</s>; the bandha is to be performed there.

children.text: badhnāti hi sirājālam adhogāmi śirojalam
children.translated_text: It binds the network of channels and the downward-moving water of the head.

children.text: tato jālaṃdharo bandhaḥ kaṇṭhaduḥkhaughanāśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is <s>jālaṃdhara bandha</s>, the destroyer of the mass of throat pains.

children.text: jālaṃdhare kṛte bandhe kaṇṭhasaṃkocalakṣaṇe
children.translated_text: When <s>jālaṃdhara bandha</s> has been made, marked by contraction of the throat,

children.text: pīyūṣaṃ na pataty agnau na ca vāyuḥ prakupyati ||
children.translated_text: the nectar does not fall into the fire, and the wind is not disturbed.

children.text: pārṣṇibhāgena saṃpīḍya yonim ākuñcayed gudam
children.translated_text: Pressing the yoni with the heel, one should contract the anus.

children.text: apānam ūrdhvam ākṛṣya mūlabandho 'bhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Drawing <s>apāna</s> upward is called <s>mūlabandha</s>.

children.text: apānaprāṇayor aikyāt kṣayān mūtrapurīṣayoḥ
children.translated_text: Through the union of <s>apāna</s> and <s>prāṇa</s>, and through the wasting away of urine and feces,

children.text: yuvā bhavati vṛddho 'pi satataṃ mūlabandhanāt ||
children.translated_text: even an old man becomes young by constant practice of <s>mūlabandha</s>.

children.text: padmāsanaṃ samāruhya samakāyaśirodharaḥ
children.translated_text: Having mounted the lotus posture, with body, head, and neck straight,

children.text: nāsāgradṛṣṭir ekānte japed oṃkāram avyayam ||
children.translated_text: with his gaze on the tip of the nose, in solitude he should repeat the imperishable syllable oṃ.

children.text: bhūr bhuvaḥ svar ime lokāḥ somasūryāgnidevatāḥ
children.translated_text: Earth, mid-space, and heaven, these worlds, and the deities moon, sun, and fire,

children.text: yasyā mātrāsu tiṣṭhanti tat paraṃ jyotir om iti ||
children.translated_text: stand in its measures; that supreme light is oṃ.

children.text: trayaḥ kālās trayo vedās trayo lokās trayaḥ sverāḥ
children.translated_text: The three times, the three Vedas, the three worlds, the three notes,

children.text: trayo devāḥ sthitā yatra tat paraṃ jyotir om iti ||
children.translated_text: and the three gods are established where that supreme light is oṃ.

children.text: kriyā cecchā tathā jñānā brāhmī raudrī ca vaiṣṇavī
children.translated_text: Action, desire, and knowledge, and the <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> powers:

children.text: tridhā śaktiḥ sthitā yatra tat paraṃ jyotir om iti ||
children.translated_text: where śakti stands threefold, that supreme light is oṃ.

children.text: ākārāś ca tathokāro makāro bindusaṃjñakaḥ
children.translated_text: The sound a, likewise the sound u, the sound m, and what is called bindu:

children.text: tisro mātrāḥ sthitā yatra tat paraṃ jyotir om iti ||
children.translated_text: where the three measures are established, that supreme light is oṃ.

children.text: vacasā taj jayed bījaṃ vapuṣā tat samabhyaset
children.translated_text: With speech he should master that seed; with the body he should practice it.

children.text: manasā tat smaren nityaṃ tat paraṃ jyotir om iti ||
children.translated_text: With the mind he should constantly remember it: that supreme light is oṃ.

children.text: śucir vāpy aśucir vāpi yo japet praṇavaṃ sadā
children.translated_text: Pure or impure, whoever always repeats the praṇava

children.text: lipyate na sa pāpena padmapattram ivāmbhasā ||
children.translated_text: is not stained by sin, like a lotus leaf by water.

children.text: cale vāte calo bindur niścale niścalo bhavet
children.translated_text: When the wind moves, bindu moves; when it is motionless, bindu becomes motionless.

children.text: yogī sthāṇutvam āpnoti tato vāyuṃ nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: The yogin obtains steadiness like a post; therefore he should restrain the wind.

children.text: yāvad vāyuḥ sthito dehe tāvaj jīvanam ucyate
children.translated_text: As long as the wind remains in the body, that is called life.

children.text: maraṇaṃ tasya niṣkrāntis tato vāyuṃ nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Its departure is death; therefore he should restrain the wind.

children.text: yāvad baddho marud dehe yāvac cittaṃ nirākulam
children.translated_text: As long as the breath is bound in the body, as long as the mind is undisturbed,

children.text: yāvad dṛṣṭir bhruvor madhye tāvat kālabhayaṃ kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as long as the gaze is between the eyebrows, how can there be fear of Time?

children.text: ataḥ kālabhayād brahmā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Because of fear of Time, <s>Brahmā</s> is devoted to prāṇāyāma,

children.text: yogino munayaś caiva tato vāyuṃ nirodhayet ||
children.translated_text: and yogins and sages as well; therefore one should restrain the wind.

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulo haṃsaḥ prayāṇaṃ kurute bahiḥ
children.translated_text: The haṃsa makes its outward journey for thirty-six finger-breadths;

children.text: vāmadakṣiṇamārgeṇa tataḥ prāṇo 'bhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: because it goes by the left and right paths, it is then called <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: śuddhim eti yadā sarvaṃ nāḍīcakraṃ malākulam
children.translated_text: When the whole circle of channels, full of impurity, becomes purified,

children.text: tadaiva jāyate yogī prāṇasaṃgrahaṇe kṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the yogin becomes capable of holding the breath.

children.text: baddhapadmāsano yogī prāṇaṃ candreṇa pūrayet
children.translated_text: Seated in the bound lotus posture, the yogin should fill the breath through the moon.

children.text: dhārayitvā yathāśakti bhūyaḥ sūryeṇa recayet ||
children.translated_text: Having retained it according to his capacity, he should again exhale through the sun.

children.text: amṛtaṃ dadhisaṃkāśaṃ gokṣīrarajatopamam
children.translated_text: Meditating on the disk of the moon, nectar-like, resembling curds,

children.text: dhyātvā candramaso bimbaṃ prāṇāyāmī sukhī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and similar to cow's milk and silver, the practitioner of prāṇāyāma becomes happy.

children.text: dakṣiṇo śvāsam ākṛṣya pūrayed udaraṃ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Drawing in the breath on the right, he should slowly fill the belly.

children.text: kumbhayitvā vidhānena puraś candreṇa recayet ||
children.translated_text: Having retained it according to rule, he should then exhale through the moon.

children.text: prajvalajjvalanajvālāpuñjam ādityamaṇḍalam
children.translated_text: Meditating on the solar orb, a mass of blazing flames of fire,

children.text: dhyātvā nābhisthitaṃ yogī prāṇāyāme sukhī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: situated in the navel, the yogin becomes happy in prāṇāyāma.

children.text: prāṇaṃ cod iḍayā pibet parimitaṃ bhūyo 'nyayā recayet pītvā piṅgalayā samīraṇam atho baddhvā tyajed vāmayā
children.translated_text: He should draw in a measured breath through <s>iḍā</s> and then exhale through the other; then, having drunk in the air through <s>piṅgalā</s> and held it, he should release it through the left.

children.text: sūryacandramasor anena vidhinā bimbadvayaṃ dhyāyataḥ śuddhā nāḍigaṇā bhavanti yamino māsatrayād ūrdhvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the restrained one who meditates on the two disks of the sun and moon in this manner, the groups of nāḍīs become purified after three months.

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ dhāraṇaṃ vāyor analasya pradīpanam
children.translated_text: The holding of the wind at will, the kindling of the fire,

children.text: nādābhivyaktir ārogyaṃ jāyate nāḍiśodhanāt ||
children.translated_text: the manifestation of inner sound, and freedom from illness arise from the purification of the nāḍīs.
